targets.authors: Shih, M., Pittinsky, T. L., & Ambady, N.
targets.title: Stereotype susceptibility: Identity salience and shifts in quantitative performance.
targets.evidence_quote: The goal of this project is to offer additional insight into the original Shih, Pittinsky, and Ambady (1999) finding that group-related stereotype awareness can affect performance and behavior on tasks related to that stereotype. We conducted a replication following Gibson, Losee, and Vitiello’s (2014) registered protocol.
targets.outcome_quote: We did not observe significant differences between Asian-primed, female-primed, and control conditions on math performance by Asian women. Further, the ordinal relations between conditions did not follow the original results – control participants performed nonsignificantly better than both Asian-primed and female-primed participants. Finally, neither awareness of these stereotypes nor identification with mathematics moderated this effect.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The discussion gives an overall negative account of the attempted stereotype-susceptibility effect and explicitly states that the group ordering does not match the original. Agreement on an auxiliary total-correct measure does not supersede this substantive verdict. Falling short of planned recruitment is a limitation, not an author verdict that the attempt cannot adjudicate.
